The issue is that `generateText` with structured output using `Output.object` fails on OpenRouter with Kimi because the model doesn't support structured output properly, resulting in a `NoOutputGeneratedError` when trying to access the output property. The `maxOutputTokens: 60` limit might be too restrictive for generating structured output.

The better approach is to skip structured output entirely for the title generation and just use plain text generation instead—that'll be more reliable across different providers. Let me check how the imports are set up to see what options are available.

The problem is clear: `Output.object()` requires the model to reliably produce structured output. OpenRouter + Kimi K2 doesn't reliably support structured/tool-call output, so no structured output is produced and accessing `output` throws `AI_NoOutputGeneratedError`. A title is simple enough that plain text generation is far more robust across providers.

The issue is that OpenRouter with Kimi K2 doesn't reliably support structured output, so the `output` field ends up empty and throws an error. I'll switch `_generateTitle` to use plain text generation instead of the structured output schema.

Type check passes. Here's what was wrong and what I changed.

## Root cause

`_generateTitle` used the AI SDK's structured output feature:

```290:294:apps/backend/src/services/agent.ts
			output: Output.object({
				schema: z.object({...}),
			}),
```

`Output.object()` relies on the model emitting a valid structured/tool-call response. OpenRouter + Kimi K2 doesn't reliably support that path, so the SDK never populates `_output`. When your code destructured `{ output }` and read it, the SDK's `output` getter threw `AI_NoOutputGeneratedError: No output generated.` — exactly the stack you saw at `agent.ts:680`.

## Fix

A conversation title is trivial enough that it doesn't need a JSON schema. I switched to plain text generation, which works across all providers:

```680:702:apps/backend/src/services/agent.ts
		const { text } = await generateText({
			model: modelResult.model,
			system:
				'Generate a short, descriptive title (3-8 words) ... Respond with the title only, without quotes or any surrounding text.',
			messages: [{ role: 'user', content: userMessageText }],
			maxOutputTokens: 60,
		});

		const title = this._normalizeTitle(text);
```

I also added a small `_normalizeTitle` helper that strips wrapping quotes/backticks and keeps only the first line (models sometimes wrap titles in quotes or add trailing chatter), and removed the now-unused `Output` and `zod` imports.

This keeps title generation robust regardless of which provider/model is selected. Type check passes.
